ashby:1password:b141ee0c-30aa-42f8-8ff7-.summary: 1Password is growing. We’ve surpassed $500M in ARR and we’re continuing to accelerate, earning a spot on the Forbes Cloud 100 for four years in a row and teaming up with iconic partners like Oracle Red Bull Racing.

sections.title: About 1Password
paras: At 1Password, we’re building the foundation for a safe, productive digital future. Our mission is to unleash employee productivity without compromising security by ensuring every identity is authentic, every application sign-in is secure, and every device is trusted. We innovated the market-leading enterprise password manager and pioneered Unified Access Management, a new cybersecurity category built for the way people and AI agents work today. As one of the most loved brands in cybersecurity, we take a human-centric approach in everything from product strategy to user experience. Over 180,000 businesses, from Fortune 100 leaders to the world’s most innovative AI companies, trust 1Password to help their teams securely adopt the SaaS and AI tools they need to do their best work.

If you're excited about the opportunity to contribute to the digital safety of millions, to work alongside a team of curious, driven individuals, and to solve hard problems in a fast-paced, dynamic environment, then we want to hear from you. Come join us and help shape a safer, simpler digital future.

As a Principal Solutions Engineer, Acceleration, you’ll help define how 1Password brings emerging technologies to market. Working across Product Management, Product Marketing, Enablement, Engineering, Sales, Customer Success, and strategic customers, you’ll validate new capabilities, shape product direction through field feedback, and turn what works into repeatable customer-facing motions.

sections.title: How we’re using AI today
paras: Across GTM, we’re transforming the way we work with AI. We expect every seller, CSM, and team member to become a power user, using it daily to work smarter and move faster. AI is already embedded in how we operate – from real-time coaching that sharpens how we sell and interact with customers, to surfacing insights that help us anticipate needs – creating more time for meaningful customer engagement. If you’re excited to reshape how you think, make decisions, and drive growth with AI, you’ll feel right at home here.
This is a remote opportunity within Canada and the US.
Note: All go-to market roles will have an in-person onboarding in Toronto.

sections.title: What we're looking for:
bullets: 8+ years of experience in customer-facing technical roles within enterprise Business-to-Business Software as a Service (B2B SaaS), including leading initiatives beyond an individual sales territory.
A track record of translating emerging technologies into customer value, repeatable field motions, and clear recommendations that shape product or go-to-market direction.
Experience partnering effectively with Product Management, Engineering, Product Marketing, and other cross-functional teams to validate capabilities and incorporate customer feedback.

Strong executive communication, storytelling, and presentation skills, with the ability to influence audiences ranging from technical practitioners to senior executives, analysts, and strategic partners.

Experience with Metrics, Economic Buyer, Decision Criteria, Decision Process, Paper Process, Identify Pain, Champion, and Competition (MEDDPICC), or a similar enterprise sales methodology, along with the ability to work autonomously and influence without direct authority.

sections.title: Bonus points for:
bullets: Experience with private previews, beta programs, or early-stage products; technical enablement and customer-facing content; or domains such as Artificial Intelligence Security (AI Security), Developer Security, Privileged Access, Software as a Service (SaaS) Manager, or Unified Access Management is preferred.
A track record of public speaking, technical writing, podcasts, analyst engagements, or other forms of technical thought leadership is also valued.

ashby:ambiencehealthcare:557575a5-6c50-4.summary:
Here at Ambience, we never set out to be just another scribe. We’re building the AI intelligence platform that restores humanity to healthcare and drives meaningful ROI for health systems across the country.

Our technology helps providers focus on delivering great care by removing the administrative burden that pulls them away from patients and away from their most impactful work. Ambience delivers real-time coding-aware documentation and clinical workflow support across ambulatory, emergency and inpatient settings at the top health systems in North America.

Our teams operate relentlessly with extreme ownership to build the best solutions for our health system partners. We value candor, positivity and deep thought — and we expect a lot from each other because we know the problems we’re solving truly matter.

sections.title: The Role
paras: As our PM Lead, Inpatient Clinical Workflows , you'll own the clinician-facing features at the heart of Ambience's inpatient platform - the documentation and chart intelligence capabilities that define the core product experience for hospitalists and specialists.

You'll be accountable for two product pillars. First, Inpatient Scribe - the documentation experience purpose-built for inpatient workflows, from admission through discharge, handling the full complexity of rounding, handoffs, multidisciplinary coordination, and discharge summaries. Second, Chart Summarization (Patient Summary & Chart Chat) - the AI-powered chart intelligence layer that enables inpatient clinicians to rapidly synthesize patient history, surface relevant clinical context, and interact conversationally with the medical record.

Done well, this role makes Ambience indispensable for inpatient clinicians - transforming how hospitalists and specialists document, synthesize, and act on clinical information across the entire care episode.

sections.title: Inpatient Scribe
bullets: Define and execute the Inpatient Scribe roadmap for hospitalists and specialists, grounded in deep understanding of inpatient documentation workflows, rounding patterns, and EHR integration requirements.
Deliver a documentation experience that handles the unique complexity of inpatient care: multi-encounter days, team-based rounding, procedure documentation, handoff notes, and discharge summaries.
Drive measurable clinician outcomes - time-to-chart, documentation completeness, reduced after-shift charting - and demonstrate clear ROI for hospital administrators.
Own inpatient quality metrics - accuracy, latency, note completeness, workflow completion rates - and systematically eliminate the pain points that drive support escalations or clinician drop-off.
Partner with Engineering and Clinical AI/ML to adapt ambient capture and note generation models to inpatient-specific language patterns, workflows, and note types.

sections.title: Chart Summarization - Patient Summary & Chart Chat
bullets: Own the product vision and roadmap for Patient Summary and Chart Chat within the inpatient setting, purpose-built for hospitalists and specialists managing complex, multi-day patient episodes.

Define the summarization experience that surfaces the right clinical context at the right moment: admission summaries, problem-oriented views, medication reconciliation context, overnight event recaps, and trend analysis across the hospital stay.
Own Chart Chat as a conversational interface to the medical record - enabling natural-language questions about patient history, labs, imaging, prior encounters, and evolving clinical trajectories.
Establish rigorous evaluation frameworks for summarization accuracy, completeness, and clinical safety in the inpatient context, partnering with Clinical AI/ML and clinical advisors.

sections.title: Must-Haves
bullets: 5+ years of product management experience with direct ownership of a vertical product line or platform, including roadmap and end-to-end product experience.
Track record of rapidly building deep domain expertise in a complex, unfamiliar domain.
Strong technical fluency - comfort with AI/ML products, API integrations, and complex system design.
Experience driving adoption in complex enterprise environments with multi-persona buying committees.
Based in SF, available to be in the office 3x/week.

ashby:astera:c3ebd007-cf6c-4c2c-9618-936.summary:
We are looking for a senior product manager to join the Discourse Graphs team, in a fully remote, fixed-term role of 12 to 18 months, paying $110,000 to $195,000 a year depending on where you are based.

Discourse Graphs is an open-source project that helps research teams write down, link and share their questions, claims and evidence, through plugins for Roam Research and Obsidian backed by a shared database. It is philanthropically funded and built by a small team across North America, Europe and India, together with the labs who pilot the tools with us.

sections.title: What you'll be doing
paras: You'll join a small and friendly distributed team of engineers, designers and researchers who are designing, building, and testing new ways of doing collaborative science. We do most of our work in writing, across many time zones, and there are no managers: engineers pull their own work from a queue, and we judge progress by what researchers do with the tools rather than by targets. We are moving from asynchronous toward pair programming, short iterations and regular retrospectives.

This role will place you in a central node of a product that is evolving with its researcher user base. We have extensive feedback from internal use as well as two years of user pilots with research labs across North America, more ideas than we can act on, a growing community of labs, and funding to do something with both. You'll shape the product strategy, working out with the founders where Discourse Graphs should go, what to prioritize, and how to get there.

Some of the questions we are considering include whether the product stays a set of plugins in Obsidian or needs a standalone app now, how it will live in researchers’ existing tools such as agentic coding interfaces, and when we will extend our use cases to adjacent areas like publication overlays and institutional research roadmapping. We’ll follow where users’ interest is strongest, while making sure the work they depend on comes first.

sections.title: About you
paras: You are drawn to the problem of how research gets documented, connected and built upon, and you'd like to spend a year or more making that easier for working scientists. You are comfortable synthesizing diverse user needs and feedback into a set of high-level priorities and concrete prototypes. Your design instinct centers usability and meeting users within their existing workflows. You like to put something early-stage in front of people and change course based on what you see, and you are at ease guiding a team as a team member. You're likely to do well in this role if you have:
bullets: Comfort soliciting and navigating user input in context of documented user flows
A habit of talking with users every week, and of showing ideas as prototypes
A way of working alongside designers and engineers rather than handing work to them
Experience working without a manager: noticing what needs doing, taking it on, and keeping others posted in writing

sections.title: Our offer
paras: The post is full-time for 12 to 18 months, either as a temporary employee of the Astera Institute or on contract at the same annual rate. It is fixed-term because our funding is, and we will be open about where the funding stands for as long as you are with us. It is fully remote, with some overlap with North American working hours, and you can also work in person at Astera in Emeryville, California. We'd like you to start as soon as you can. Pay is $110,000 to $195,000 a year, depending on where you are based. We also offer:
bullets: A flexible approach to working hours and remote working
Astera-sponsored health, vision and dental benefits for employees
Onboarding help from peer product teams

sections.title: How we hire
paras: We start with a 30-minute call to get to know each other, with the last ten minutes for your questions. Next is a working session of up to 90 minutes with two of us on a real piece of our product work, in place of a take-home task. After that you'll talk with the founders about where you think the product should go, and finally we'll ask for two references, from an engineer and a designer you have worked with.

A bachelor's degree

Exceptional writing that is clear, credible, and evidence-based, with first drafts that need little rework

ashby:canvas-medical:9fa7e1bb-6ba3-4b8d-.summary:
Canvas Medical is accelerating everyday medicine with an EMR platform built for healthcare automation. We create modern, elegant front- and back-end tooling to enable new ways for developers and clinicians to integrate data, automate workflows, and collaborate to solve healthcare's toughest challenges. In doing so we advance our mission to give care teams superpowers with software.

Canvas is institutionally backed by some of the greatest technology investors in the world (funded notable health tech companies such as GoodRx, Oscar Health, and Hims & Hers Health).

ashby:centivo:673fdc4e-426e-43ae-8555-44.summary:

sections.title: Executive Account Leadership & Renewals
bullets: Lead the end-to-end renewal strategy for each national account, developing a client-specific approach that demonstrates measurable plan performance, validates savings against benchmarks, and positions Centivo for long-term retention.

Design and deliver executive-level renewal presentations and business reviews that translate complex data — including claims analytics, cost benchmarking, clinical outcomes, and member engagement metrics — into a compelling, consultative narrative tailored to each client’s goals.

Personally oversee the identification, tracking, and resolution of high-stakes client issues, including claims discrepancies, executive-level member escalations, and provider disputes, by mobilizing the right resources and maintaining transparent client communication throughout.

Collaborate with internal analytics, clinical, and product teams to develop account-specific reporting that reflects each client’s defined success metrics and organizational priorities.
Monitor emerging data signals—including high-cost claimants, utilization patterns, and care gap trends—and translate findings into actionable recommendations for plan sponsors.

ashby:civilgrid:932fa162-00f3-494d-98e8-.summary:

Our platform consolidates utility records, geotechnical and environmental data, paving moratoriums, and jurisdictional requirements directly from 3,000+ utilities, agencies, and municipalities with full chain-of-custody documentation. Teams at PG&E, Mark Thomas, and dozens of leading engineering firms use CivilGrid to cut research time by up to 88%, reduce project costs, prevent dig-ins, and accelerate delivery on the projects that keep communities running.

sections.title: ABOUT CIVILGRID
paras: We're a venture-backed Series A startup tackling a $4.7T US infrastructure market that has been underserved by software for decades. Founded by industry insiders, each with 10+ years in utilities and civil engineering, we move fast, ship work that matters, and stay close to the customers and field teams we build for.

sections.title: WHY THIS ROLE

sections.title: WHAT YOU'LL DO
bullets: Own the roadmap for your product area end to end — from customer discovery and validation through launch, iteration, and measurement
Partner with the Head of Product to translate company strategy into a focused, prioritized plan for your area, and represent that plan to the leadership team
Partner closely with engineering as a true thought partner: drive execution, work through trade-offs, and ship on fast cycles
Stay close to our customers to deeply understand their workflows and the decisions our platform needs to power
Lead and grow a small team of PMs: hire, mentor, and manage while staying hands-on in the work yourself
Champion a default-to-shipping culture: get product into customers' hands fast, then learn and iterate

You’ve shipped multiple iterations of successful B2B products
You can go deep on technical detail with engineers and zoom out to strategy with executives in the same hour
Start up ready - you’re autonomous, move fast, and take initiative without being asked

ashby:coderabbit:427dffaf-9661-47c7-8155.summary:
CodeRabbit is the governance and control layer for agentic software development, helping engineering teams trust the code they ship. AI can generate code faster than people can review and understand it. Teams still need to know whether each change solves the right problem, fits their architecture, and is safe to ship.

We provide independent validation grounded in codebase context and team standards, giving people the evidence they need to judge what should ship. Across Review, Triage, Explain, and Secure, our platform challenges changes before merge, prioritizes pull requests by value, impact, and risk, explains what changed and why it matters, and monitors the codebase for security vulnerabilities after merge.

CodeRabbit serves nearly 20,000 customers and supports approximately 300,000 open-source repositories, performing over 2 million code reviews each week. Our $143M Series C,…

sections.title: About the role
paras: Product at CodeRabbit sits at the intersection of developer empathy, frontier AI capabilities, and real commercial stakes. As a Product Manager, you will shape how millions of developers experience AI-powered code review across IDEs, Git platforms, the CLI, and the web — surfaces where the playbook hasn't been written yet and the models improve under your feet every quarter.

Our work decides whether CodeRabbit feels like noise or like a trusted teammate: whether a developer acts on a review comment, adopts an agentic workflow, or brings CodeRabbit to their whole organization. You will live close to both the customer and the model — talking to developers weekly, prototyping with AI tools yourself, and translating what's newly possible into products people rely on.

We are hiring across all levels, and we mean it. If you are early in your product career with sharp instincts and a bias for shipping, we will give you real ownership from week one. If you are a seasoned product leader or former founder who has taken products from zero to category-defining scale, we will give you problems worthy of that experience — and room to shape the product organization itself. We will calibrate scope, title, and compensation to you, not the other way around.

sections.title: What you'll do
paras: Depending on your experience, you will own a surface, a product line, or the roadmap itself. Across levels, the work looks like this:
bullets: Own problems end-to-end. Drive discovery, definition, and delivery — from customer conversations and data analysis through specs, launch, and iteration — for products developers use every day.

Stay close to the customer. Build relationships with the developers and engineering leaders who use CodeRabbit, run feedback loops with our largest customers, and turn what you hear into what we build.
Stay close to the model. Understand what frontier models can do today and where they're heading, and design products for the capabilities arriving next — not just the ones already here.
Prototype to learn. Use AI tools to build and validate ideas yourself before committing engineering resources. The cheapest way to answer a product question is often to build the answer.
Ship fast and measure honestly. Get work in front of users quickly, define what success looks like before launch, and let adoption and retention — not opinions — settle debates.
Partner deeply with engineering, design, and go-to-market. Work fluently with technical teams on how things get built, and with sales and marketing on how they land.
Bring structure to ambiguity. Much of this space has no precedent. You'll frame the problem, propose the path, and rally the team around it rather than waiting for direction.
For senior folks: raise the bar. Define product strategy across surfaces, mentor other PMs, and help build the product culture and team around you.

sections.title: What we're looking for
bullets: Sharp product judgment. You form clear points of view from customer conversations, usage data, and your own use of the product — and you change them when the evidence says to. This is the core of the role, at every level.
You ship. You would rather get something in front of users this week than perfect it for a month, and you take pride in what happens after launch, not just the launch itself.
You're AI-native in how you work. You already use AI tools daily to extend what you can do — prototyping, analyzing, writing — and you have informed opinions about where these tools fall short.

You're technical enough to be dangerous. You can go deep with engineers on how something works, read a pull request, and understand why a model behaves the way it does. An engineering background helps but isn't required.
You communicate to drive decisions. You write clearly, bring clarity out of complexity, and influence without authority — whether the audience is an engineer, a customer, or the executive team.
You're energized by ambiguity. Emerging AI product surfaces have few conventions. You see that as the opportunity, not the obstacle.

ashby:cohere:068e9b49-e22b-493c-824f-0cc.summary:

sections.title: Operating Principles
paras: Deepgram is a research company that productizes as fast as possible. Four Operating Principles shape how we think, decide, and work together:
We look for people who already work this way, and these principles shape how we grow and evaluate our team.
bullets: Compress before you communicate. You think it through first, then lead with the bottom line.
Resist entropy. You question what already exists before adding more process or tools.
Solve the category. You fix recurring problems at the source, not one case at a time.
Work at the frontier. You go after problems no one has solved yet.

sections.title: AI-First by Default
paras: We build AI that millions of people talk to, and we run the company the same way. AI is how we centralize work here, and is core to how we operate.
That means more than using the tools. We expect you to:

We judge AI by what it helps you deliver and whether you stand behind the result, not by how often you use it. In interviews, expect to walk us through a workflow you built and where you drew the line between AI and your own judgment.
bullets: Build, not just use. Design your own workflows and agents, and use AI to remove whole categories of work instead of doing the same work faster.
Own the output. AI can speed up the work. It doesn’t make anyone less accountable for it. You understand, verify, and stand behind everything you share, including what an agent produces for you.
Spend the time you get back at the frontier. The capacity AI creates goes toward problems no one has solved yet.
Keep pace. Models and tools change every month, and so will your work. You adopt what’s new quickly and drop what no longer earns its place.

ashby:granted:7d86af1f-280e-46c9-8dbb-97.summary:
The US healthcare system is complex, error-prone, and financially draining. Medical bills and insurance coverage shouldn't be this hard to navigate. At Granted, we're building the one solution every American can turn to for help.

Thanks to AI and new regulations, Granted can fight claim denials, correct billing errors, negotiate bills, and make coverage easier to understand — saving people time, money, and stress. Our goal is simple: to be the #1 platform that empowers all Americans to take charge of their healthcare.

sections.title: 🧭 About the Role
paras: Granted lowers people's healthcare costs and cuts down on admin and stress. We're building the AI-native patient financial OS — the first purpose-built company working entirely on the user's side of the healthcare system, unequivocally advocating for consumers.

The hook is bill lowering. People come to us when they have a medical bill they can't afford or don't understand. Granted checks it — catches errors, overcharges, and denials, secures financial assistance, and negotiates with providers. Our Healthcare Advocates (HAs) and AI agents work those cases together.

This is primarily a strategy role, but you're not afraid of getting in the weeds of case-work. You've seen medical billing from inside the system, and you use that judgment to find what's systematically leaving money on the table — then turn it into the rules, playbooks, and product logic that make every case better. You'll look across hundreds of cases, spot the patterns an individual advocate wouldn't, and decide what Granted should build, change, or automate next.

sections.title: 🛠 What You'll Do
bullets: Review uploaded bills each week and analyze: lowerable or not, how, with what confidence, and what data would change your mind. This analysis tunes our bill checker and intake.

Look across open and closed cases to find systematic opportunities — where advocates or AI agents are leaving savings on the table — and translate the patterns into strategy, process changes, and product input.
Be the escalation point for VIP, high-complexity, and specialized cases.
Act as strategic partner to Product as the domain owner on our AI bill analyzer — shaping what we build and how we automate.
Partner on the playbooks, training, and onboarding that lets quality scale as the HA team grows (led with CX, not owned solo).
Make sure features that touch HA workflows land with the context advocates need.
Publish weekly reports on opportunities for the HA team.
Stretch: turn user and advocate pain points from casework into input for the roadmap

sections.title: Must-haves:
bullets: 4+ years of work experience in a complex consumer industry.
Experience in a strategy, product, or operations role at a tech company where you built something from scratch.

Fluency in how a medical bill gets built, from CPT, ICD-10, and HCPCS coding to the EOB, and how to lower one through appeals, financial assistance policies, No Surprises Act protections, and tactful negotiations.
Comfort in a fast-moving startup: scrappy, sharp, and quick to ramp on new products and tools.

sections.title: Nice-to-haves:
bullets: Time spent on both the provider and payer sides of a bill.
Hands-on work with AI or agentic tools in a billing, clinical, or ops setting.
Experience working directly with patients, such as advocacy, care navigation, or patient financial services.
Experience training or leading a team of billers, advocates, or specialists.

Strong understanding of work-cell design, machine safety standards, and risk assessment.
Track record of taking systems through FAT, commissioning, and SAT.

The payment operations lead who spent their morning chasing down why a batch of transactions failed now expects to ask a question and get an answer. AI has collapsed the distance between wanting something done and it being done.

You'll own the AI assistant that works on a merchant's behalf across Adyen – one that can find and read their data, provide insights, take real actions, and know where its limits are. You'll build some of what it can do yourself, and build the foundation that lets teams across Adyen contribute the rest – reporting and insights, disputes, configurations, and everything that follows. sections.title: Unlocking AI Agents for the Finance Admin
paras: Companies buy Brex to run their spend, and the person on the hook for that is the finance admin — a controller, an accounting manager, a finance ops lead. Their job comes down to two things they can never quite get ahead of: making sure money is being spent compliantly and documented in time to close the books, and knowing where the company's money is actually going.

Today they do both by hand, at a scale that doesn't work. Roughly 4% of travel and entertainment spend is out of policy — for a company spending $10M a year, that's $400K in violations, duplicates, missing receipts, and overspend. Most companies never find it, because finding it means a human reading transactions one at a time. The ones who do find it either staff a review team or bolt on a separate audit product with its own login. On the other side, the questions that actually matter — where did spend grow this quarter, which team is drifting, what's driving the number — sit behind a queue for an analyst, or a spreadsheet the admin builds themselves at month-end. Nobody is continuously watching.
The AI team is working to give every finance admin two people they can't hire today: an auditor and a business analyst.

sections.title: What you'll do
paras: You'll work on our core AI team building agents for the finance admin and own one of these end to end. You'll set its product direction, decide which capabilities to build and how they should behave, and spend real time with controllers and finance teams to learn what they'll actually trust an agent to do on their behalf. From there you go as deep as it takes to make it real: shaping agent behavior, writing and iterating prompts, designing the evals that prove it works, and digging into traces when it doesn't. You'll partner closely with engineering, design, and research, and you'll set the quality bar for agents that customers rely on to keep their spend clean and their numbers right.

Your work will span three priorities. You will evolve card demand planning into a rigorous, repeatable forecasting process. You will build on existing research and analytical prototypes to establish reliable measurement of product activation and the member lifecycle, from account opening and first direct deposit through adoption, engagement, and retention. Establish historical backtesting, benchmark comparisons, forecast bias and error monitoring, and uncertainty estimates. Investigate misses and continuously improve performance.
Partner with PMM, Card Operations, and Finance to translate forecasts into planning scenarios and assess implications for inventory, supplier lead times, cost, and service risk.
Build reproducible forecasting workflows with documented assumptions, stakeholder inputs, monitoring, and clear ownership.

Evaluate proposed operating metrics, including Activated Member Rate, assessing product selection, thresholds, observation windows, sensitivity, and relationships with downstream engagement and retention.
Balance timely operational signals with cohort maturity and analytical validity. Distinguish predictive relationships from causal evidence and identify where further validation is needed.
Identify friction and drop-off across onboarding and cross-product journeys, size opportunities, and recommend actions to improve activation and sustained use.
Partner with Enterprise Data & Metrics and source-data owners to develop tested dbt models, historical backfills, governed metric definitions, and reliable Hex reporting.
Establish metric governance, versioning, and historical comparability as products, eligibility rules, and definitions evolve.
Create recurring monitoring and business-review mechanisms that help PMM understand performance and distinguish changes in member behavior from the incremental impact of its initiatives.

sections.title: Connect member research with quantitative evidence

Use behavioral data, segmentation, funnel analysis, and statistical methods to assess the prevalence of research findings and how they differ across member groups.
Combine qualitative and quantitative evidence to guide positioning, messaging, onboarding, and product adoption strategies.
Design, power, and interpret experiments to evaluate these strategies, coordinating analytical ownership with Product and Growth Analytics.
Apply appropriate causal inference methods when randomization is not feasible, clearly communicating assumptions, uncertainty, and limitations.
Identify where behavioral evidence and research findings diverge, and recommend follow-up analysis or research to resolve the gaps.

greenhouse:jetsonhome:4258017009.summary:
Jetson is on a mission to accelerate the transition of 100 million homes across North America away from fossil fuels toward sustainable energy use. We believe in a future that is 100% electric and 100% better.

Homes are one of the largest sources of carbon emissions, yet adoption of solutions like heat pumps remains slow due to cost and complexity. Jetson is solving this by building the first fully vertically integrated home electrification company — making clean energy simple, transparent, and affordable.

We rely heavily on technology, automation, and data to scale this impact. At Jetson, we value people who are excellent at their craft, curious about new tools (including AI), and motivated to continuously improve how work gets done.

sections.title: The Opportunity
paras: Jetson is looking for a Product Marketing Specialist to own how our new products go to market — from positioning and messaging to launch execution and performance tracking. This is a high-ownership role at the intersection of product, growth, and revenue. You will define how each product is introduced to the world, ensure our CRM and analytics infrastructure reflects what's live in each market, and coordinate across paid, organic, and growth channels to make launches land. You'll be the connective tissue between product roadmap and marketing results.

sections.title: What You'll Do
bullets: Own end-to-end go-to-market strategy for new product launches — defining target segments, positioning, messaging hierarchy, and channel mix, then driving execution from announcement through adoption.
Develop and maintain product positioning and messaging frameworks that translate technical features into clear, benefit-led stories tailored to distinct buyer personas and geographies

Set up and manage HubSpot infrastructure to support product launches: creating custom properties, configuring lifecycle stages, and designing dashboards that track launch performance across markets and geographies

Coordinate paid, organic, and growth channels for each launch — briefing channel owners with positioning, defining experiments, aligning creative and copy to the messaging framework, and tracking which channels drive pipeline velocity
Manage analysis and reporting workflows, including win-loss research and competitor positioning tracking, to provide actionable insights for various stakeholders.
Identify process and tooling gaps in how launches are planned and tracked; build repeatable playbooks and automate workflows using AI tools to increase the team's capacity.
Collaborate with product and sales to align on launch readiness, enablement materials, and feedback loops.

Be held accountable to performance targets — success in this role is measured against clear KPIs including pipeline contribution, launch-attributed revenue, channel performance, and adoption metrics by product and geography.

sections.title: What You Will Bring
bullets: 4–7 years of product marketing experience, with at least 2 years owning go-to-market launches at a high-growth startup or fast-moving consumer brand; experience in home services, energy, or hardware is a plus
Demonstrated expertise in positioning and messaging — you can write a positioning statement, build a messaging framework, and translate both into briefs that align a cross-functional team

Hands-on HubSpot experience: you know how to architect custom properties and deal pipelines for new products, configure lifecycle stages and workflows, build segmented lists for multi-geo rollouts, and create dashboards that surface the metrics that matter

Proven ability to coordinate across paid, growth, and organic channels for a launch — you understand how each channel works well enough to write a tight brief, review creative, and hold partners accountable to the messaging

Experience launching products or campaigns in multiple geographies — including localizing messaging, adapting competitive positioning by market, and setting up tracking that distinguishes performance by region
Strong qualitative research skills, you can synthesize findings into clear strategic recommendations
Comfort working with data — you can pull reports, analyze funnel metrics, build a launch scorecard, and identify where pipeline is stalling and why
Genuine interest in AI and automation: you actively look for tools and workflows that eliminate manual work, and you've already used AI to improve how you research, write, or run campaigns

greenhouse:jfrog:8140207.summary: At JFrog, we’re reinventing DevOps to help the world’s greatest companies innovate -- and we want you along for the ride. This is a special place with a unique combination of brilliance, spirit and just all-around great people. Here, if you’re willing to do more, your career can take off. And since software plays a central role in everyone’s lives, you’ll be part of an important mission. Thousands of customers, including the majority of the Fortune 100, trust JFrog to manage, accelerate, and secure their software delivery from code to production -- a concept we call “liquid software.” Wouldn't it be amazing if you could join us in our journey?

sections.title: As an Associate Account Manager, Revenue Retention, in JFrog you will...
bullets: Scale the renewals process by architecting accurate quotes and opportunities across a targeted global portfolio.
Drive operational excellence by collaborating with Finance, Legal, and Deal Desk to ensure 100% contract accuracy and compliance.

Optimize Salesforce data integrity to provide real-time visibility into renewal health and territory performance, recognizing that clean, current data is the direct input to the AI-driven renewal risk scoring this team runs on.

Accelerate business growth by identifying expansion opportunities and providing actionable insights during the renewal cycle using AI-assisted signal review (Gong call analysis, renewal risk scoring) to surface expansion opportunities before they show up in a standard pipeline review.
Recognize strategic deal signals and streamline the customer experience by orchestrating high-touch communications and owning contract and legal-adjacent processes end-to-end.
Approach the renewal motion as something actively evolving with AI-assisted tooling, ready to take on higher-complexity, higher-touch accounts as routine tiers become more automated.

sections.title: To be an Associate Account Manager, Revenue Retention in JFrog you need...
bullets: A minimum of 4 years of relevant experience in account management, renewals, or sales operations within a SaaS environment.
Proven track record of managing high-volume portfolios and meeting tight deadlines with exceptional attention to detail.

Advanced proficiency in Salesforce (SFDC) and the MS Office Suite, particularly Excel, including working deal math independently: discount deltas, co-term pricing across tiers, and monthly-vs-annual savings comparisons.

Demonstrated problem-solving skills with the ability to navigate complex internal processes and cross-functional dependencies, including contract and legal workflow literacy (JSA, DPA, NDA, compliance routing).
Strong verbal and written communication skills to effectively engage with both internal stakeholders and external customer liaisons.

Experience in a fast-paced, high-growth technical environment where adaptability and a “Froggy” spirit are essential, with working depth on the JFrog platform itself (Xray, edge nodes, tiering) enough to handle a technical objection without a one-line script.
AI fluency for non-technical, customer-facing work: using AI to accelerate research and drafting, then verifying the output before treating it as finished.

greenhouse:justworks:8264370.summary:
At Justworks, you’ll enjoy a welcoming and casual environment, great benefits, wellness program offerings, company retreats, and the ability to interact with and learn from leaders in the startup community. We work hard and care about our most prized asset - our people.

We’re helping businesses get off the ground by enabling them to focus on running their business. We solve HR issues. We’re data-driven and never stop iterating. If you’d like to work in a supportive, entrepreneurial environment, are interested in building something meaningful and having fun while doing it, we’d love to hear from you.

We're united by shared goals and shared motivations at Justworks. These are best summed up in our company values, which are reflected in our product and in our team.

sections.title: Who We Are
paras: If this sounds like you, you’ll fit right in.

sections.title: Who You Are
paras: Product Marketing defines how Justworks wins —shaping our narrative, informing decisions, and driving growth through pricing, positioning, and GTM systems. The Customer Journeys team owns how customers enter, convert, and expand across the platform. We are the connective tissue between the platform and the go-to-market motion.

We are seeking a Senior Product Marketing Manager, Growth with a GM mentality and a direct line to business outcomes. Your work will directly affect funnel conversion, net revenue retention, and customer lifetime value—whether you’re shaping how SMB prospects discover and choose Justworks, or defining the signals and strategies that drive customers from single-product to multi-product adoption.

This role is built for a PMM who combines customer obsession with analytical rigor and a hacker’s mentality for finding growth—someone who moves fast on data and knows that the best insights come from spending time with customers, not just dashboards.

sections.title: Journey & Lifecycle Design
bullets: Own strategy and messaging across the full customer lifecycle—from acquisition (point of entry through conversion and activation) to expansion (progression across products and platform)—translating ICP definitions into entry points, progression paths, and conversion strategies across the funnel.

Design and optimize acquisition journeys that move prospects from first touch through conversion, and expansion journeys that drive customers toward multi-product adoption—reducing time-to-value and time-to-expansion across both self-serve and sales-assisted motions.

Define lifecycle stages, key moments, and behavioral triggers that shape how customers experience and progress through each stage—producing journey blueprints the broader GTM system can execute against.
Partner with Pricing & Packaging to ensure journey strategy reinforces platform positioning and pricing communication at key conversion and upsell moments.

sections.title: Growth Strategy & Execution
bullets: Partner with Product, Growth Marketing, Revenue, and other PMM teams to design and prioritize growth strategies across the funnel—focusing on the highest-impact opportunities to improve acquisition efficiency, conversion velocity, and expansion revenue.
Define how and when customers grow across the platform: target audiences, messaging by lifecycle stage, and the behavioral signals and triggers that drive movement between products and stages.
Build growth strategy and prioritization frameworks that guide where the team invests—balancing entry path optimization, ICP-based segment targeting, and expansion opportunity sizing.
Serve as the business owner for your funnel area: set goals, track performance, communicate results to leadership, and continuously raise the bar on what good looks like.

greenhouse:motivity:4373005009.summary:
Motivity is looking for a Product Marketing Manager to own how our product is positioned, launched, and sold across a wide market, from solo BCBA-owned practices to national operators with 50+ locations and a formal procurement process.

This is our first dedicated product marketing hire. The role spans positioning and messaging, launch strategy, enablement, competitive intelligence, and customer insight, working closely with product, sales, and marketing to better communicate our unique approach and the value we bring to the market.

The right person for this role is a strong writer who can turn a complex, regulated product into a sentence a busy clinic owner understands on the first read. They are comfortable owning scope and ambiguity, and they build positioning from direct customer conversations rather than from a spreadsheet.

sections.title: Positioning and messaging
bullets: Own how Motivity is positioned across a wide range of buyers — from a solo BCBA owner with three learners to a national operator with 50+ locations. Turn what our product does into what it means for a Clinical Director versus a CFO versus the RBT using it in session.
Build the category narrative for our move upmarket so enterprise buyers can answer questions about multi-site governance, audit readiness, and migration at scale.

sections.title: Launches and go-to-market
bullets: Own product launch strategy and execution end to end: the brief, the narrative, the sequencing, the channels, and the post-launch read on whether any of it worked. Turn the roadmap into external stories.
Maintain the customer-facing changelog and the plain-language product source of truth that everything else (campaign copy, customer-facing decks, website, release comms) draws from.

sections.title: Sales enablement
bullets: Build the assets that move deals: one-pagers, pitch decks, demo scripts, solution briefs, competitive battlecards, talk tracks, and proof points.
Collaborate and align with Sales and Product through internal launch training that makes sure what Sales says matches what Marketing publishes.

sections.title: Competitive intelligence
bullets: Own the competitive picture in ABA software and turn it into something our team can use. Our competitors range from entrenched all-in-one incumbents to point solutions for data collection and billing, and displacement conversations are a large share of how we win.

Anticipate where competitors are heading, not just where they are. Sharpen our differentiation accordingly, including the honest version: where we're genuinely better, and where we need to acknowledge a gap and reframe.

greenhouse:onetrust:8328582.summary: OneTrust’s mission is to enable innovation through the responsible use of data and AI. We believe that ensuring data is trusted shouldn’t slow teams down—it should accelerate what’s possible. This led us to develop the first technology platform for responsible data use in 2016. Today, with AI representing the latest and most impactful expansion of data yet, OneTrust is once again redefining what responsible innovation looks like. OneTrust, the AI‑Ready Governance Platform™, unifies regulatory intelligence, automation, and connected governance workflows so businesses can continue to move at the speed of AI while ensuring good governance to prevent data misuse at scale. Trusted by thousands of organizations worldwide, OneTrust is shaping the future where trusted data becomes a transformative force for business and society.

sections.title: The Challenge
paras: OneTrust is hiring a Director of Product Management to lead our AI Platform. You will be accountable for getting customers to turn AI on, use it heavily, and create business value from that usage. AI is built into the OneTrust platform. The question that matters most is how much customers use it once it’s on. You will own that answer, and lead three product teams: infrastructure, quality and trust, and agent building and reasoning. This is a strategic role, and a hands-on one. You will prototype directly with modern AI development and design tools. When a team is stuck, you can open the tools and show them what great looks like.

sections.title: Your Mission
paras: You are accountable for three outcomes, judged together: engagement, adoption, and revenue.
bullets: Engagement (first priority): Increase AI usage per customer that has access to AI and has turned it on.
Adoption: Move customers from having access to AI to turning it on, working with Sales, Customer Success, and Marketing.
Revenue: AI-attributed revenue within existing solution sales, a shared goal with Sales and Finance.
Set strategy and roadmap across infrastructure, quality and trust, and agent building and reasoning, and make the tradeoffs between them.
Design AI capabilities to scale across the OneTrust platform and partner ecosystem.
Work with Product Marketing, Sales, Sales Engineering, Partnerships, Customer Success, and Finance on roadmap and go-to-market.
Build and lead a team of product managers and product leaders with clear accountability and high standards.
Run customer listening, including the Customer Advisory Board and voice-of-customer programs, so the roadmap follows real usage.

sections.title: Who You Are
paras: You build, not just manage. You have grown usage of an enterprise platform or AI product, not just launched it. You can set multi-year strategy and also work through hard product problems with a team. You think in platforms, not point solutions, and you know how to lead in a complex enterprise where trust and scale matter.

sections.title: THE ROLE
paras: As Director of Product Management for Subsystems, you will lead the strategic vision and portfolio execution for the hardware and networking infrastructure powering Everpure’s FlashArray and FlashBlade platforms. Operating as an influential player-coach, you will build and empower a team of Subsystem PMs while partnering directly with VP leadership, Engineering, and Supply Chain to set operational objectives and budgets. At Real Chemistry, making the world a healthier place isn’t just an aspiration—it’s our everyday reality. Our drive to transform healthcare is informed by our blend of deep scientific expertise, human-centered creativity, and AI-driven insights, fostering a unique environment where innovation thrives and our people are impact-obsessed. Location: Remote, New York City, or Oakland, CA

Recidiviz is thrilled to be hiring a Senior Product Marketing Manager to join our External Affairs team! We're a small, fast-moving group that is changing the narrative about what is possible in the criminal justice system. That's where you come in. We’re looking for a strategic storyteller who can define how corrections agencies understand what Recidiviz builds, and who wants to change what government expects from its software along the way. You'll build demand for technology that keeps agencies in control, keeps pace with innovation, and is measured by the change it creates: safer communities, happier staff, and more people thriving after release.

sections.title: About the role
paras: As Senior Product Marketing Manager, you'll own the product narrative and messaging for Recidiviz's corrections products and services, including our offender management system (OMS) modules and policy analytics offerings. You will build a deep understanding of the people who decide when and how to modernize agency technology: corrections directors, deputy directors, CIOs, and procurement leaders. You'll decide how to reach them and shape how they understand what we build and why they should care.

You're not just positioning Recidiviz products. You're shifting what the market expects from corrections technology, building demand for flexible, modular infrastructure, better contracts, interoperability, open standards, and iterative delivery.

The same is true for AI. Corrections leaders are being pitched AI from every direction, and the space is shifting fast. You'll help them pursue AI innovation and responsible AI together: building demand for tools that are safe, transparent, and accountable, helping buyers ask the right questions about every AI opportunity in front of them, and giving them the confidence to move forward even as the landscape changes.

sections.title: Core responsibilities
bullets: Own the product narrative: Build the positioning and messaging frameworks for our corrections products and services, so decision makers understand what each tool does and why it matters to them. Make the product story on recidiviz.org clear and compelling for that audience.

Make outcomes the measure: Set the expectation that corrections software should drive results, not only track activity. Turn evidence from our partner states into impact narratives and case studies that are specific, credible, and hard to ignore.

Set the standard for responsible AI: Build demand for AI that is both innovative and safe. Create frameworks, buyer questions, and content that help agency leaders evaluate AI opportunities from any vendor, and feel confident making decisions in a fast-moving space.
Launch what we build: Partner with Product and our go-to-market teams to plan and run launches for new products and features, with consistent messaging from first announcement through adoption.
Lead market intelligence: Track the corrections technology landscape and make sure our teams can articulate Recidiviz's differentiation clearly and accurately.
Prepare the story for the stage: Own the product narrative talk at our annual Partner Summit, and create the talks, workshop submissions, and materials we bring to industry conferences.

sections.title: Wild success
paras: Here are a few things you might accomplish in your first year at Recidiviz that would demonstrate wild success in this role:
bullets: The market speaks a new language of outcomes: Corrections agencies and vendors alike start describing their work in terms of the results it drives, and you hear your framing echoed in conference talks, trade coverage, and vendor marketing.
Agencies start buying differently: Agency leaders ask for outcomes, interoperability, and modular, iterative delivery, rather than a decade-long list of fixed requirements.

Buyers ask sharper questions about AI: Agency leaders use your frameworks to evaluate AI tools, and responsible AI requirements show up alongside innovation goals in how they scope and buy technology.
Our teams reach for your work first: The narrative, case studies, and competitive positioning you build become the materials our teams use instinctively in every conversation with an agency leader.

sections.title: Position Summary
paras: This consultancy will focus on expanding the implementation into additional facilities and strengthening the ongoing implementation of the project in 13 regions. The Consultant will coordinate the selection and assessment of facilities, training of mentors and mentees (facility focal points), and support the execution of regular mentorship to make the facilities ready to safely prevent, detect, and respond to public health emergencies while maintaining essential healthcare services.

Five consultants are planned for this assignment: four regional implementation consultants and one data-management Consultant who will support implementation across all regions. Regional assignments will be confirmed based on project needs, consultant suitability, language and contextual considerations, and feasibility. Any subsequent reassignment to another region or group of facilities will be discussed and mutually agreed with the Consultant. The consultants will work closely with the Principal Manager for Prevent Epidemics and the Epidemic Ready Primary Health Care (ERPHC) Technical Advisor to achieve all deliverables.

sections.title: Core Tasks and Activities
bullets: Develop concept notes that outline the delivery approach and plans for the specific regions assigned to each Consultant by the ERPHC Technical Advisor.
Work closely with the assigned regions’ health bureau/regional public health institute and EPHI to identify private facilities to enroll in the project.
Train assessors on RTSL’s capacity assessment tools and approach, support the data collection process, and analyze each region’s health facility data.
In collaboration with regional PHI/RHB, support the selection of mentors and mentees and facilitate their training in line with the RTSL training package.
Support the mentorship process to enable enrolled private health facilities to achieve significant improvement from their respective baseline scores on PHEM and IPC indicators.
Review the mentorship data submitted by mentors each month and give mentors feedback after each mentorship week so that course correction can be done promptly
Conduct data-quality spot checks and supportive supervisions at selected facilities, as needed, to verify that mentorship data submitted by mentors matches facility records.
Organize performance review meetings to track improvements and share lessons learned.

sections.title: Contract Deliverables
bullets: Facility and mentor/mentee selection completed in the assigned region, and mentors and mentees (facility IPC/PHEM focal points) trained according to a phased implementation schedule agreed during onboarding.
Baseline capacity assessments completed for enrolled facilities, followed by implementation of structured mentorship and collection, analysis, and visualization of mentorship data using RTSL tools.
Monthly mentorship follow-up completed, including monitoring continuity of mentorship, data submission, and reporting, with feedback provided to mentors as needed.
Regional engagement and buy-in secured from the respective Regional Public Health Institutes (RPHIs) and/or Regional Health Bureaus (RHBs) to support project implementation and sustainability.
Endline assessment is completed. Significant improvement gains from baseline are achieved for all facilities in the overall PHEM and IPC scores. A 20% gain is ideal.

The Independent Contractor will prepare and submit monthly progress reports summarizing implementation progress, mentorship performance, facility improvements, challenges, corrective actions, and next steps.

sections.title: Contract Management
paras: The Consultant will submit deliverables to the ERPHC Technical Advisor for review and acceptance. The Principal Manager for Prevent Epidemics will manage the contract and approve invoices.

You will co-own the follow-through, from confirming specifications to handing off to onboarding, and help turn what we learn into talk tracks and enablement that others can use.

bullets: Lead client discovery conversations about large data Extracts: how each one is used, what question it answers, how often it is needed, where it goes downstream, and who relies on it.

Identify overlap and redundancy across a client’s Extracts and recommend the most efficient path for each, including consolidating into a SPINS Share (aggregated and/or trended), trimming or splitting to fit SPINS Extracts, Managed Extracts, SPINS Intelligence, or discontinuing .
Capture and confirm data specifications at the Extract level (measures, geographies, time periods and products), prepare first-version configurations, and keep client records accurate and current.
Co-lead follow-through with the Senior Sales Engineer and Customer Success Managers, including follow-up sessions, specification confirmation, and handoff to onboarding .
Guide clients on data volume and cell-count trade- offs so deliveries are sized to real needs, and recognize when a request expands scope and should route to a commercial conversation.
Communicate candidly when guidance is still evolving, log open questions, and escalate to Product, commercial and Data Governance partners for resolution.

greenhouse:ww:5275450008.summary: Weight Watchers is the global leader in science-backed weight management, offering an integrated support system built for the GLP-1 era that combines scientific expertise, medication, cutting-edge technology, and human connection. With more than 60 years of experience, Weight Watchers is the most studied commercial weight management program in the world, delivered through its No. 1 U.S. doctor-recommended weight-loss program. Its holistic, personalized approach also includes U.S.-based clinical interventions and access to GLP-1 medications when clinically appropriate, and a global network of coaches and community support. Since 1963, the company has led with science to deliver its members the personalized support they need to reach and sustain their goals. Members can access these solutions directly, or through Weight Watchers for Business’ full-spectrum platform for employers, health…

sections.title: What You'll Do
paras: Members come to WeightWatchers at very different moments — starting a new program, considering a GLP-1, settling into a routine, hitting a plateau, coming back after time away. Our challenge is to meet each of them where they are. We're taking the magic of our in-person workshops, the accountability and connection that come from showing up alongside other people, and extending it with experiences only possible in a digital product. We're blending clinical expertise, coaching, and self-serve tools into a program that works for each person, on the premise that the best plan is the one someone can actually stick with. There is no one-size-fits-all, so the experience has to adapt to each member's goals, needs, and lifestyle.

You'll own how that experience holds together as a coherent whole: a consistent product point of view, personalized to where a member actually is in their journey, expressed in the daily surfaces they return to for food, guidance, reassurance, and support.

This is a high-change environment, and you'll have real room to shape what our member experience becomes, with outsized influence on a business serving millions of people. Your specific area of focus will be set based on team needs and your background, and will evolve as the product does. We're looking for someone who can deliver impact across different surfaces and problem types. You will:
bullets: Set the vision and strategy for your area, in service of the whole. Define what great looks like for your surfaces, and make sure they connect into one coherent, personalized member experience.
Design for real, daily behavior. Build experiences members want to open every day, that adapt to where they are in their journey, and that blend digital with workshops, coaching, and community.
Make content-rich experiences feel personal. Help members find, understand, and act on a lot of guidance, food data, and programming — dynamically, based on their needs — without overwhelming them.
Make smart bets. Size the odds, move fast on reversible decisions, think big when the upside is there, and change course quickly when the evidence changes.
Deliver measurable impact. Own outcomes in sustained engagement, retention, and topline revenue, balancing short term and long term objectives.
Challenge the status quo. Question inherited assumptions about how the product works, propose bolder alternatives, and be willing to be wrong in public.
Run a high-velocity experimentation practice. Form sharp hypotheses, ship tests fast, read results honestly, and change your mind when the data says to.

Raise the bar for the team. Set an example on product judgment, writing, and prioritization, and help define how this team operates as it grows. Bring curiosity about how AI can make us faster and make the product better.

sections.title: Who You Are
bullets: A high-agency owner: You don't wait to be told what to do. When something needs to happen, you make it happen, even if it isn’t in your direct remit. You are relentless and creative in pursuit of impact.
Energized by ambiguity and change: You thrive without a playbook and don't need clarity before you move. You would rather shape a fast-moving product with outsized impact than run a well-defined one.

A bold risk-taker with good judgment: You know when to move fast, when to think big, and when to take a swing. You question inherited assumptions, make calls with incomplete information, and are comfortable being wrong in public, and you can tell us what you learned .

A systems thinker: You see how the pieces connect and understand how a change to one surface, program, or moment in a member's journey ripples through the rest. You keep an experience coherent across teams you don't manage.

Grounded in user behavior: You spend real time with the people you build for, talking to them and watching how they use the product, and you design from observed behavior, not assumptions. You understand what drives habit change.

Rigorous with data: You define your own metrics, build your own funnels and readouts, and design experiments that produce clean reads. You have results you can quantify and credibly attribute to your work, and you're skeptical of your own conclusions.

lever:getcircuit:767b1d61-1e49-4f44-aa87.summary:
Circuit is the AI execution layer for the physical economy.

Industrial and manufacturing enterprises run on expertise: the hard-won knowledge of how complex products are engineered, configured, sold, and supported. That expertise is scarce, slow to transfer, and walking out the door as a generation of experts retires. It lives in PDFs, spreadsheets, and the heads of a few people, and the hardest technical decisions wait on whoever happens to know.

Circuit puts expert judgment in everyone's hands. We capture how the best people make critical technical decisions and turn it into agents that do the judgment-heavy work, so anyone, regardless of skill level, can make the right call, from quote to install and support, with the accuracy these environments demand.

sections.title: About Circuit
paras: Circuit is built by operators. Our leadership team has built and scaled real industrial companies, and we are already live in production with category-leading manufacturers. We are not bolting AI onto an old playbook. We are building the layer that runs the last mile of how the physical economy executes.

sections.title: The Role
paras: As Sr. Product Marketing Manager at Circuit, you'll help shape how our products are positioned, launched, and sold. You'll own messaging for Circuit's core use cases, run the launch motion that carries each release into the market, and arm Sales and Customer Success with the positioning, tools, and proof they need to win.

This is an individual contributor role with real ownership. You'll run positioning and messaging for your areas end to end, from customer and competitive research through launch, enablement, and web. You'll partner with Product on how we talk about what we build, and with Sales and CS to make sure that story lands in every deal.

This is a builder role. You'll help establish the launch framework, enablement system, and measurement for product marketing at Circuit while staying deeply hands-on with execution. Because marketing at Circuit is still taking shape, you'll also take on broader marketing work as needed, including social, content, and executive ghostwriting.
